# Which memory, when, at what cost (sample data, not a result)

> **SAMPLE DATA. THIS IS NOT A BENCHMARK RESULT AND NOT A RECOMMENDATION.**
> This guide was generated from `20261031T135234525464Z-sample-fake`, a sample run in which at least one of the chat model, the judge and the embeddings was fake (`LLM_PROVIDER=fake`, `JUDGE_PROVIDER=fake`, `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fake`). The fake model can only copy from its prompt, so every number below describes the harness and the format of this guide. None of them says anything about a real model or a real memory backend, and the costs are what the recorded fake tokens would cost at the listed price. Do not quote them. The guide is regenerated from a real run when one is published (`make run-v2`, then `make publish`).

Source: [`aggregate.json`](../results/runs/20261031T135234525464Z-sample-fake/aggregate.json) and [`manifest.json`](../results/runs/20261031T135234525464Z-sample-fake/manifest.json) of run `20261031T135234525464Z-sample-fake`. 2 runs of 20 turns, checkpoints 10, 20, answering model `fake-memory-v1`, judge `fake-judge-v1`, embeddings `fake-hashing-384`, k = 2, 4. Cost is recorded tokens at $3.00 per million input tokens and $15.00 per million output tokens (`fake-memory-v1`, source: pricing.yaml (mirrors anthropic-claude-4.5-sonnet), checked 2026-10-30). List price, no prompt caching discount.

How to read the figures:

- **Recall** is the mean of per-run recall with a 95% Student t interval over runs. It leaves out the `abstention` and `sensitive` categories, which are shown on their own under recall by category. With few runs the interval is wide. Two backends whose intervals overlap are not separated by this run; that is not the same as being equal.
- **Cost per conversation** covers the answering calls and memory upkeep (summary rewrites, fact extraction). **Cost per correct recall** is conversation spend plus headline probe spend, divided by the headline probes answered correctly.
- **Memory latency** is the time the memory itself adds to a turn: the read before the answer and the write after it. For `summary` and `mem0` the write includes an LLM call.

## Pick this when (rule output on sample data, not advice)

The lines below show what the rules print. They were computed from fake-model numbers and are not advice about any backend.

Each line is produced by a fixed rule in `src/site/guide.py` from the tables that follow. The rules compare 95% intervals, so they say "not separated" far more often than "better".

- (sample) **Highest recall:** `buffer` at 79.5% [0, 100].
- (sample) **This run does not separate any backend from the best on recall:** every interval overlaps the best one's. On this evidence the choice comes down to cost and latency; more runs would be needed to rank recall.
- (sample) **Pick `qdrant@k2` when you want the cheapest backend whose recall is not separated from the best:** $0.0081 per conversation at 73.2% [51, 96] recall. The highest-recall backend, `buffer`, costs $0.0173 per conversation, 2.1 times as much.
- (sample) **Pick `qdrant@k2` when the unit you pay for is a correct answer:** $0.0020 per correct recall, the lowest of all backends, at 73.2% [51, 96] recall.
- (sample) **Pick `buffer` when the memory must add the least time to a turn** (among the backends not separated from the best): 0.0 ms read plus 0.0 ms write at p50. Compare that with the answering call's p50 of 0.2 ms before treating it as a reason.
- (sample) **For single facts stated once** (`extraction`): 9 backends tied (all except `summary`) and scored highest, 100% (up to 8 probes each; see the table for the intervals, which are wide).
- (sample) **For facts that are corrected later** (`update`): 9 backends tied (all except `summary`) and scored highest, 100% (up to 3 probes each; see the table for the intervals, which are wide).
- (sample) **For date arithmetic across turns** (`temporal`): every backend scored 0%, so this category does not tell them apart (up to 2 probes each).
- (sample) **For combining two facts from different turns** (`multi_hop`): `buffer` scored highest, 50% (up to 2 probes each; see the table for the intervals, which are wide).
- (sample) **For saying so when the user never told it (highest rate means it makes things up least)** (`abstention`): `summary` scored highest, 50% (up to 4 probes each; see the table for the intervals, which are wide).
- (sample) **Retrieval depth for `qdrant`:** k = 2 had the highest recall (73.2% [51, 96]). It is the smallest depth swept, and no larger depth scored higher.
- (sample) **Retrieval depth for `pgvector`:** k = 2 had the highest recall (73.2% [51, 96]). It is the smallest depth swept, and no larger depth scored higher.
- (sample) **Retrieval depth for `langgraph_store`:** k = 2 had the highest recall (73.2% [51, 96]). It is the smallest depth swept, and no larger depth scored higher.
- (sample) **Retrieval depth for `mem0`:** k = 2 had the highest recall (73.2% [51, 96]). It is the smallest depth swept, and no larger depth scored higher.

## What this guide does not cover
